```{r}
#| label: load-packages
#| include: false

library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
```

## Exercise

### Part 1

We provide you with an Excel file `EH2011.xlsx` that contains gene expression data for the nine most highly variable genes in a pancreas cancer gene expression dataset (downloaded from <https://portal.gdc.cancer.gov/projects/TCGA-PAAD>), as well as metadata for the individual samples and genes.

- Import the gene expression matrix from the Excel file into the R session as a `tibble`.
  Assign it to an object named `exprs_assay`.

```{r}
library(readxl)
excel_sheets("data/EH2011.xlsx")
exprs_assay <- read_xlsx("data/EH2011.xlsx", "exprs")
exprs_assay
```

- Reshape the gene expression matrix in a tidy format.
  Assign it to a new object `exprs_assay_long`.

```{r}
exprs_assay_long <- exprs_assay %>%
  pivot_longer(-gene, names_to = "sample", values_to = "exprs")
exprs_assay_long
```

- Draw a histogram of gene expression levels for each gene in a separate facet.

```{r}
ggplot(exprs_assay_long, aes(exprs)) +
  geom_histogram(fill = "grey", color = "black", bins = 40) +
  facet_wrap(~gene) +
  cowplot::theme_cowplot()
```

## Exercise

### Part 2

- Import the sample metadata from the Excel file into the R session as a `tibble`.
  Assign it to an object named `sample_info`.

```{r}
excel_sheets("data/EH2011.xlsx")
sample_info <- read_xlsx("data/EH2011.xlsx", "sample_info")
sample_info
```

> Metadata key:
> 
> [NIH AJCC staging system](https://www.cancer.gov/about-cancer/diagnosis-staging/staging)
> 
> - sex: male or female
> - grade: how abnormal the cancer cells and tissue look under a microscope
> - T: size of the tumor and any spread of cancer into nearby tissue
> - N: spread of cancer to nearby lymph nodes
> - M: metastasis (spread of cancer to other parts of the body)
> - vital_status: living or deceased
> - sample_type: tumour or normal

- Convert each of the columns above to factors.

```{r}
sample_info <- sample_info %>%
  mutate(across(
    c(sex, grade, T, N, M, vital_status, sample_type),
    list(as.factor),
    .names = "{.col}"))
sample_info
```

- Combine sample information with gene expression data.
  Assign the output to `exprs_sampleinfo`.

```{r}
exprs_sampleinfo <- sample_info %>%
  left_join(exprs_assay_long, c("unique_patient_ID" = "sample"))
exprs_sampleinfo
```

## Exercise

### Part 3

- Identify the gene with the largest absolute difference in expression between male and female patients.

```{r}
exprs_sampleinfo %>% 
  group_by(sex, gene) %>% 
  summarise(exprs = mean(exprs)) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = sex, values_from = exprs) %>% 
  mutate(F_minus_M = F - M) %>% 
  arrange(desc(abs(F_minus_M)))
```

- Visualise the expression of that gene in the two sexes using a geom of your choice.
  Consider colouring and faceting by other metadata (e.g., `grade` and `T`).

```{r}
table_for_ggplot <- exprs_sampleinfo %>% 
  filter(gene == "XIST")
table_for_ggplot
```

```{r}
ggplot(table_for_ggplot, aes(grade, exprs, colour = T)) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~ sex)
```

- Draw a heat map of all nine genes.
  Remove labels as well as ticks for the x-axis.
  Remove the panel grid and background.

```{r}
ggplot(exprs_sampleinfo, aes(unique_patient_ID, gene, fill = exprs)) +
  geom_raster() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid = element_blank(), panel.background = element_blank())
```

- Repeat the heat map, faceting samples by sex.

```{r}
# Copy the code chunk above and edit as needed
ggplot(exprs_sampleinfo, aes(unique_patient_ID, gene, fill = exprs)) +
  geom_raster() + 
  facet_wrap(~sex, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid = element_blank(), panel.background = element_blank())
```

## Bonus exercise

### Part 1

- Import the provided read count data table `allsamples_counts.tsv.gz`. This table was produced by a tool called featureCounts.

```{r}
infile <- "data/allsamples_counts.tsv.gz"
featurecounts_table <- read_tsv(infile, comment="#")
glimpse(featurecounts_table)
```

- Create a new tibble called `counts` that contains only the column containing the gene ID `Geneid` and the columns containing the read counts (those ending in ".bam").
- Remove the ".bam" suffix from the sample column names.

```{r}
counts <- featurecounts_table %>% 
  select(Geneid | ends_with(".bam")) %>% 
  rename_with(~ str_remove(.x, "\\.bam$"))
```

- Create a matrix that contains the count data converted into CPM (counts per million reads) with the row names as the gene IDs and the column names as the sample IDs.
- Check if the matrix contains any NAs.

```{r}
cpm_matrix <- counts %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      ends_with(".bam"),
      ~ (.x / sum(.x, na.rm = TRUE)) * 1e6
    )
  ) %>% 
  column_to_rownames("Geneid") %>% 
  as.matrix()

# CPM derived from featureCounts output should not have any NA values, but it is good to check this:
if (anyNA(cpm_matrix)) {
  warning("The CPM table contains NA values.")
}
```

- Convert the CPM to log2 CPM (you will need to add a pseudocount of 1 before log transformation).

```{r}
# log2 transform
cpm_matrix <- log2(cpm_matrix + 1)
```

- Transpose the cpm_matrix so that the genes are along the columns, use t().
- Use prcomp() to run PCA, center the data but do not scale it.
- Calculate the percent variance explained by each principal component.

```{r}
# PCA expects samples in rows and genes in columns
cpm_matrix <- t(cpm_matrix)

# Run PCA
pca <- prcomp(cpm_matrix, center = TRUE, scale. = FALSE)

percent_var <- (pca$sdev^2 / sum(pca$sdev^2)) * 100

percent_var[1:5]
```

- Convert the in PCA scores (the coordinates of your samples in principal component space) to a data.frame. The PCA scores are stored in pca$x.
- Add a column called `sample` which has the name of each sample (without the ".bam" suffix).
- Use ggplot to create a scatter plot of PC1 vs. PC2.
- Bonus: add the percent variance explained by PC1 and PC2 to the x- and y-axis labels.

```{r}
pca_df <- as.data.frame(pca$x)

pca_df$sample <- rownames(pca_df) %>% str_replace(fixed(".bam"), "")

ggplot(pca_df, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, label = sample)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_text(vjust = -0.8) +
  labs(
    x = paste0("PC1 (", round(percent_var[1], 1), "%)"),
    y = paste0("PC2 (", round(percent_var[2], 1), "%)")
  ) +
  theme_classic()
```

- Read in the metadata tsv file, `PRJEB18572_sample_info.tsv`.

```{r}
metadata <- read_tsv("data/PRJEB18572_sample_info.tsv")
metadata
```

- Add the metadata to the the pca_df, using the common information (sample identity) to join.

```{r}
pca_df <- pca_df %>% left_join(metadata, join_by(sample == sample_id))
```

- Use ggplot to create a scatter plot of PC1 vs. PC2.
- colour by cell type.
- set the shape to vary by genotype.

```{r}
ggplot(pca_df, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color=cell_type, shape=genotype)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  labs(
    x = paste0("PC1 (", round(percent_var[1], 1), "%)"),
    y = paste0("PC2 (", round(percent_var[2], 1), "%)")
  ) +
  theme_classic()
```
